description: Returns who came to ONE post/page — the same numbers the owner sees in the editor’s Traffic tab, the Your Content list and the posts list. Three counts that are NEVER summed, because they are different populations on different clocks: `ai` is readers an AI assistant sent (people), `bots` is crawler/agent fetches of the page or its Markdown copy (machines — refused requests, PROVEN fakes, scripts and WordPress sites left out and counted apart; `verified` says whether each bot was checked), and `search` is the connected engine’s own report for the page over ITS OWN dates (null when it reported nothing, or no engine is connected). `ai` and `bots` cover the last `window` days. ⚠️ When `matching` is true, older traffic is still being matched to its pages and the numbers may rise — say so rather than quote them as final. When `pageViews` is false, page visits are not recorded and `bots` counts only Markdown reads.
name: agentimus-read-post-traffic

total.description: Readers AI assistants sent to this page.

label.description: The bot, as the Request Log names it.

last.description: Its most recent read of this page, GMT "Y-m-d H:i:s".

verified.description: TRUE when at least one of its reads passed the operator’s own check. FALSE means not checked — not fake.

leftOut.description: Requests for this page from PROVEN fakes or refused at the door — not reads, so not in total. read-request-log with this post lists them with their status.

more.description: Bots counted in total but left out of byBot.

notReaders.description: Requests for this page from scripts and command-line tools, or from WordPress sites (this site's own included) — not a bot reading the page, so not in total.

total.description: Bot reads of this page and its Markdown copy.

daily.description: Every day of the window, oldest first, zeros included. For each read with its time, call read-request-log with this post.

knownSince.description: When not empty: the first day bot reads can be placed on a page at all — reads before it were logged without their page, so `bots` covers fewer days than `window`. Say so when you quote it.

matching.description: TRUE while traffic logged before per-page counting existed is still being matched to its pages.

pageViews.description: Whether bot visits to pages are recorded. FALSE ⇒ bots counts only reads of the Markdown copy.

recording.description: Whether visits are being recorded at all. FALSE ⇒ ai and bots are not measured, whatever they read.

end.description: Last day of the engine’s range.

partial.description: TRUE: summed from the page’s reported searches, which leave out rare and private ones — can sit a little under the engine’s own page total.

queries.description: The searches that brought people here, most clicks first (at most five).

start.description: First day of the engine’s range.

window.description: Days the ai and bots counts cover, today included.

title: Get one page’s traffic
